articles.title: US COURT RULES GOOGLE WILL NOT HAVE TO SELL AD EXCHANGE AFTER LOSING ANTITRUST CASE
articles.summary: Google's ad tech dominance will largely remain intact despite the DOJ proving that it illegally restricted competition in parts of the online ad market. The court rejected the government's push to force Google to sell its ad exchange, avoiding a remedy that could have disrupted its broader advertising business. Google will likely face fines and business practice changes, but the exact penalties remain sealed for now. The outcome shows that even after three major antitrust losses, Google retains substantial control over digital advertising and can continue investing aggressively in emerging markets such as AI.

articles.title: ‘A CRISIS OF AUTHENTICITY': THE TRUTH ABOUT FOOD INFLUENCERS
articles.summary: Positive coverage in food influencing is less a preference than an economic default, since restaurants that stop offering free meals or payment quickly see coverage dry up. That system still drives real reach, with Instagram Reels revenue growing from about $2 billion in 2022 to a projected $50 billion and roughly half of Instagram's time now spent on them. Most restaurant influencers still don't get paid well, with typical per-post rates staying in the low hundreds to low thousands and Instagram not paying for views at all. Viewers have noticed the pattern, and experts predict today's relentlessly positive accounts will lose ground to more critical voices.

articles.title: WIN REPORT: HOW SUPPLY-SIDE CRO LIFTED SIGN-UPS BY 15%
articles.summary: Supply-side CRO can unlock major marketplace growth by optimizing for the actual intent of people who provide capacity, not just the customers who buy. A tutoring marketplace found that many tutor recruitment visitors came from job search sites, so it replaced a generic registration form with a real student job request, clear job details, pay information, and “apply” language. The change increased tutor applications by 15%, or about 20,000 additional tutors in the first year. Supply-side improvements may not show immediate revenue, but they can strengthen marketplace capacity and create an overlooked source of high-impact conversion gains.

articles.title: THE IMPACT OF CONTENT FRESHNESS ON AI CITATIONS
articles.summary: Content cited by AI assistants runs 25.7% fresher than what ranks organically on Google, with roughly half of all citations tracing to material updated in the last 13 weeks. That edge decays fast, with a median citation half-life of about 4.5 weeks across platforms. Retrieval systems re-rank the entire candidate pool on every query rather than relying on a persistent ranking, so recency becomes an early filter for weeding out sources that might already be wrong. Perplexity and Grok weigh it most heavily, while Google's AI Overviews stay tied to core search and actually skew slightly older.

articles.title: CAPTURE ATTENTION THAT LASTS WITH 15-SECOND ENGAGED VIDEO VIEWS
articles.summary: Reddit launched a 15-second Engaged Video Views goal that optimizes video ads toward users likely to watch for at least 15 seconds or to completion. It's designed for longer-form creative such as product demos and testimonials, with advertisers paying only for qualifying views. Alpha testers saw average gains of 51% in 15-second view-through rate and 71% in completion rate. The feature is now available globally in public beta, with split testing available to compare it against 6-second views.

articles.title: BUILD VS. BUY: MARKETING TOOLS IN THE VIBE CODE ERA
articles.summary: AI is changing how marketing teams should think about build vs. buy. Teams should build when customization or proprietary data creates an advantage, and buy when vendors handle complex infrastructure that's expensive to maintain. They also warn against letting vibe-coded tools become one-off projects that only one person uses. When evaluating software, ask what would break if you canceled it and whether you're buying the product or simply a way to organize data you already own.

articles.title: CREATORS AS A SALES ENGINE: HOW CHINA IS RETHINKING THE ENTIRE CUSTOMER JOURNEY
articles.summary: China is showing how creators are becoming part of the sales infrastructure, not just a communications channel. On platforms like Rednote, creator content can intercept search, shape product research, trigger retargeting, and drive purchases through livestreams and in-platform ecommerce. The result is a more connected customer journey where content, search, community, and commerce work together rather than as separate channels. As platforms like TikTok expand into commerce, this model offers a preview of how social could take on more of the customer journey in Western markets.

articles.title: STICKI ROLLS IS TURNING STICKERS INTO THE NEW SOCIAL CURRENCY
articles.summary: Sticki Rolls turns stickers into social currency by designing the product around sharing and self-expression. It has expanded into bracelets, sticker books, pendants, and bag charms that fans can collect and show off. The brand also works with creators who shaped its original collections and uses unexpected spaces like nail salons to bring the product into beauty and fashion. Its pop-ups further turn fans into participants, with activities like sticker manicures and BFF bracelet-making.

articles.title: SKIMS MARKETING STRATEGY: KIM KARDASHIAN'S BILLION-DOLLAR BRAND
articles.summary: Behind SKIMS' celebrity headlines is a disciplined owned-channel operation, with the brand sending roughly five emails a week announcing drops, restocks, and retail collaborations. Before a major collection ships, SKIMS also seeds unboxing packages to thousands of micro-influencers across a range of body types and skin tones, producing unedited fit videos that build trust faster than a polished ad could. Both tactics are cheap, repeatable, and aimed at an audience that already opted in, the opposite of the celebrity-cash-grab reputation the brand is often given credit for.
